column1: # Graph-Owned-Test-Artifacts M3 -- disposition of every runtime compiler flow
# THIS DETECTOR FINDS in a declared test source.
# WHAT "EVERY" MEANS HERE, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.  The set is exactly what
# static, regex-plus-dataflow scan over test sources.  It is not a claim about
# every runtime compile that exists.  A flow this detector cannot see is not
# dispositioned below and is not refused by the gate, and the detector has
# known blind spots (a compiler reached through a helper in another module; a
# command assembled across procs; a spelling absent from COMPILER_PATTERNS).
# Read every count in this file, and the `test_no_test_body_helper_compilation`
# assertion that consumes it, with that scope attached.
# THAT SCOPE IS NOT THEORETICAL.  Two spellings walked straight through the
# patterns until this change: `nim check`, which had no pattern at all, and a
# compile verb carried in a fragment beginning with a space
# (`nimExe & " c --compileOnly ..."`), which the verb pattern's anchor
# excluded -- the repository's most common spelling, not an exotic one.  A
# third hole sat one layer down: a compiler fragment on a CONTINUATION LINE of
# an open `execCmdEx(` was matched and then discarded, because the line has no
# executor token of its own and `let (a, b) =` defeats the assignment tracker.
# Ten declared test sources hid a real compiler spawn behind those three.
# A FOURTH was introduced BY THE FIX for the second and caught before it shipped,
# which is the honest reason to expect more rather than fewer.  Separating nim's
# switches from this repository's CLI flags was first attempted on PUNCTUATION:
# `--name:value` for nim, `--name=value` for everything else.  Nim accepts both
# `" c --out=x"` walked straight through the fix for `" c --out:x"`.  Widening
# that rule to accept `=` would have been worse than the bug it fixed: 40
# declared test sources here spell `--mode=` (62 occurrences across 42 .nim
# files -- the other two are the CLI's own usage text in
# libs/repro_cli_support and an imported, non-declared fixture module
# scans -- every one the PRODUCT, none a compile) and all 40 would have been
# condemned.  DERIVATION, so this survives re-scanning rather than being taken
# on an earlier header's word -- at 8a8cf16b4:
# yields 62 lines over 42 files; "declared" means the file appears in
# Every one of the 62 lines in the 40 declared sources also carries the `check`
# verb -- the only three `--mode=` lines in the tree that do not are in
# libs/repro_cli_support, which this check does not scan.
# (An earlier revision of this header said 20 sources / 31 occurrences / 22
# files.  Those were attributed rather than measured; the command above is the
# measurement, and it makes the point more strongly, not less.)  The rule now
# keys on nim's switch VOCABULARY, extracted from `processSwitch`'s own case
# block, which holds under either separator and admits neither `--mode` nor
# The gate is only as wide as its patterns, so widening them is how the list
# tests/unit/test_graph_owned_test_artifacts.py pins the closed spellings in BOTH
# directions -- four arms require a real compile to be detected, one requires
# `repro check --mode=pre-push` NOT to be.  A rule satisfying only one direction
# sorted in C byte order.  Enforced by scripts/check_test_body_helper_compilation.py.
# PROVENANCE.  Re-derived at reprobuild 64e719c9f (origin/dev merged) from the
# --write-inventory-sources` and byte-identical to the checked-in artifact:
# The milestone's 63 / 64 / 65 figures are from July 2026 and no longer
# describe any tree.  The build-dependent reprobuild-suite-m0-inventory.json is
# stale by construction; do not reconcile against it.
# 94 is the BEFORE figure and is what this list dispositions: the 87 sources
# the tree still detects, plus the 7 `graph-owned` sources whose flows this
# change removed.  Every row below is one of those 94.  The seven stay -- that is the whole
# point of the `graph-owned` verdict.  It is not a stale-row bug, and the audit
# knows the difference: a row with any OTHER verdict whose flow has disappeared
# (The previous header said 84 / 77 against the pre-fix patterns.  The delta is
# the ten sources those patterns could not see, not ten new tests.)
# BUCKET TALLY at the commit above, from the rows below:
# THE CLASS LABEL DOES NOT PARTITION MIGRATE FROM KEEP.  Reviewing only the 12
# graph-fixture entries would have missed t_ct_test_runner_full_suite_parity,
# which compiles a checked-in fixture exactly like its four siblings but is
# labelled `integration` because it also needs the repro binary.  Re-counted at
# 8a8cf16b4 against the class field of the source inventory, joining every row
# below to `staticallyDetectedRuntimeCompilerFlows[].class` by source path: of
# the 41 rows now carrying `graph-owned` or `migrate-pending`, exactly ONE is
# and 7 are ABSENT from the detected set entirely -- those are the seven
# `graph-owned` rows, whose flows this change removed, so the inventory has no
# class to offer for them.  22 of the 41 sit under tests/integration/ (20 of
# `migrate-pending` rows alone the split is exactly 27 / 6 / 1.
# (An earlier revision of this header said "34 are `integration` and 6 are
# `platform/destructive`".  That rolled the seven `graph-owned` rows into
# `integration` and then reported the migrate-pending TOTAL, 34, as if it were
# an integration count.  The structural point above is unaffected and is what
# the sentence is for.)  Every entry below was read individually.
#   graph-owned          Migrated: a repro.nim edge builds the artifact and the
#                        test's execute edge declares it. Re-acquiring a compiler
#                        spawn is a FAILURE, not a new baseline row.
#   product-api          The flow is a call into reprobuild's own compilation API.
#                        The product compiles; that is the subject. M3 says to
#   compiler-is-subject  The compiler's own behaviour -- its diagnostics, its
#                        argv, its timing, or the fact that it ran at all -- is
#   dynamic-source       The compiled text is generated at run time, so there is
#                        no static file for an edge to name.
#   mutated-artifact     The produced binary is destructively rewritten by the
#                        test; a shared read-only graph output cannot serve.
#   optional-host-tool   A host-installed packer/installer, not a compiler
#                        producing a helper binary; the test skips without it.
#   migrate-pending      ACCEPTED DEBT. This entry should become graph-owned and
#                        has not been done. Every row says what blocks it.
# THE APPLIED CRITERION, stated once so it can be checked against the rows:
# IF THE COMPILED TEXT NEVER VARIES, THE ROW IS migrate-pending, whatever the
# text is spelled in.  A fixed `const` written verbatim is a checked-in fixture
# that has not been checked in yet; calling it `dynamic-source` parks migration
# debt in a KEEP bucket, where it stops being counted.  `dynamic-source` is for
# text that actually differs run to run -- a host path baked in, a per-index or
# per-fixture substitution, a template rendered from live data.
# ELEVEN ROWS WERE MOVED under that criterion (all were `dynamic-source`):
# (Nim-only, nothing blocks them but the work);
# concatenation of module-level consts and whose drift comes from three -d:
# defines, i.e. three nim.c(defines = ...) edges; and eight whose fixed const
# is compiled with `cc`, blocked exactly like the three below.
# STANDING BLOCKER, counted rather than estimated: repro.nim has no C-compiler
# build edge at all -- every nim.c(...) edge is Nim-only -- so a fixture built
# with cc/gcc/clang cannot be lifted into the graph today no matter how static
# its source is. That blocks ELEVEN of the 34 migrate-pending rows:
# (The first is blocked only in part: its `nim c` half is liftable today, its
# `clang -c` half is not.) The other twenty-three are blocked on nothing but
# t_b0_runquota_repro_nim_compiles, whose rows name their own blockers.
# TEN of the KEEP rows also compile C, and those are a separate matter -- they
# WOULD stay KEEP even if a C edge existed: 3 compiler-is-subject (the
# compile's outcome is the assertion, and one of those compiles must FAIL),
# 3 dynamic-source, 4 mutated-artifact (the binary is rewritten in place).
# Two of the three dynamic-source rows substitute into the C text (a host gcc
# path in t_e2e_codetracer_in_place_project_file, a per-package version in
# t_e2e_local_reprobuild_project_build, is MIXED and is the one row here whose
# label fits only part of it: its C fixtures ARE fixed consts, but the file's
# other flow is a `nim check` over a reprobuild.nim written at run time whose
# FAILURE is asserted, which no graph edge can express.  Nothing actionable is
# parked -- its C half is blocked on the missing C edge either way.
# DERIVATION, stated so the count survives re-scanning.  Re-derived at
# 8a8cf16b4 by joining each KEEP row to its record in
# whether any `matches[].patterns` entry is one of the four C-compiler pattern
# rows qualify.  THE BOUNDARY ROW IS NAMED because the basis decides it:
# is in only through `dynamic-c-compiler`, which matches
# run time rather than spelled.  Drop that pattern and the count is nine, with
# 2 compiler-is-subject; it is kept here because a compiler reached through a
# variable is still a compiler.  The same join over the `migrate-pending` rows
# returns exactly the eleven listed above, which is an independent check on
# that list.  (Earlier revisions of this header said seventeen -- counting the
# eight rows moved above as if they were staying -- then ten, then nine.  Nine
# was the narrow basis reported as if it were the stated one.)

column3: Built by edge reprobuild.test_fixtures.ct_shim_fixture_baseline. Its docstring lists 'the binary compiles cleanly' as assertion 1; the graph edge does not drop that assertion, it relocates it -- a fixture that stops compiling fails the edge and the suite cannot run. The remaining assertions are about the binary's stdout shape and exit code.

Built by edge reprobuild.test_fixtures.ct_shim_fixture_m4_parity_suite, shared with t_ct_test_runner_partition_file_mode. The subject is the pass/fail/skip parity of two RUNNERS over one binary; compiling that binary is materialization. Classified 'integration' by the inventory only because it needs the repro binary -- proof that the class label does not partition migrate from keep.
Built by edge reprobuild.test_fixtures.ct_shim_fixture_m4_parity_suite, shared with the parity test. The subject is ct-test-runner's --partition file: handling, not the compile.

Built by edge reprobuild.test_fixtures.ct_shim_fixture_protocol_three_tests, shared with t_test_binary_run_one_writes_result_file. The subject is the --list-json protocol document the fixture emits at run time. NOT the trap that spared t_smoke_ct_test_unittest_parallel: that test IMPORTS the shim so its own binary is the artifact under test, whereas this one only executes a separate binary built from a checked-in fixture.

Built by edge reprobuild.test_fixtures.ct_shim_fixture_protocol_three_tests, shared with t_every_test_binary_speaks_list_json_protocol. Six cases across the two tests previously compiled a private copy each into per-case scratch dirs to stop one case relinking a binary another was executing; one read-only graph artifact removes the race instead of working around it.

The compiler's ACCEPT/REJECT verdict is the assertion: probes() (:91) returns six probes carrying mustCompile true/false and the loop (:275) fails when compiled != probe.mustCompile. FOUR OF THE SIX MUST NOT COMPILE, so no build edge can produce them -- an edge that fails is a broken build, not a passing test. Newly detected: the fragment is ' c --threads:on ...' on a continuation line of an open execCmdEx( call (:268-271), which the pre-fix detector matched and then discarded.

The compiler's DIAGNOSTIC is the assertion: the helper (:196) runs nim check on a generated interface module and returns (ok, output) so the test can assert a specific REFUSAL message. A graph edge cannot produce an artifact whose compile is required to fail. Newly detected: 'nim check' had no pattern at all before this change.

quoteShell(candle)/quoteShell(light) drive WiX to synthesize an MSI fixture from generated .wxs. The tool is a host-installed installer packer, not a compiler producing a helper binary; the test skips when it is absent, and a graph edge for it could only be expressed with a host-local assumption about where WiX lives.
quoteShell(iscc) drives the Inno Setup compiler over a generated .iss to synthesize an installer fixture; skips when iscc is off PATH. Same reasoning as t_builtin_adapter_installer.

The compiler's behaviour against a genuinely read-only source tree is the subject -- the defect this pins is an OSError unwinding out of the Nim VM. compileConsumer (:193) is asserted BOTH ways: compiled.ok (:253) and 'not compiled.ok' (:308). The gate needs TWO GENERATIONS whose build-ids differ, and it needs the second one to appear WHILE the first is still mapped. buildLib (:128) links generation one with -Wl,--build-id=sha1 (:130); the rebuild command (:157-159) compiles generation two and 'mv's it over the mapped path, and the running probe executes it through REBUILD_CMD (:171). The gate then asserts the two ids differ (:193) -- if they did not there would be nothing to detect. A build edge produces one artifact per output path, not a replacement performed mid-execution, so the temporal ordering is unexpressible as a declared input. The same call builds a DELIBERATELY DEGENERATE artifact: buildLib(libV1, noIdLibPath, false) (:311) passes -Wl,--build-id=none so the object has no '.note.gnu.build-id' at all (asserted :312-313) and 'elf-build-id-absent' is the expected refusal (:331). An edge that emitted an unverifiable library would be a broken build, not a passing test. The payoff assertion is that with verification off the stale file yields the live entry of a DIFFERENT function (:259) -- the corruption the check prevents.

Executes the actual patchableCompileFlags(ReproHcr()) through GCC and Clang with -fcf-protection=full/none. Compiler-generated ENDBR64/NOP sled bytes, relocated patchable entries and the resulting production planner acceptance/refusal are the assertions, including the GCC/Clang difference and Clang CET refusal. The compiles measure the toolchain/profile contract, not merely helper availability; the test spawns them itself, so this is not product-api.

What the toolchain EMITS is the subject; the reader is only the instrument. Two generations of one C translation unit are compiled with -ffunction-sections/-fdata-sections (:136-139) so that the three diff outcomes at :191-196 are real compiler output rather than constructed bytes, and the unsupported relocations at :241-270 are GOT-relative and TLS entries GCC chose to emit on its own. g++ compiles a real C++ TU for SHT_GROUP/GRP_COMDAT (:327-329), cross-checked against readelf (:335-340). The patchable arm compiles gen1Source TWICE -- once with patchableCompileFlags(ReproHcr()) (:56, asserted :353-354, compiled :356-359) and once without -- and asserts patchableEntrySectionCount > 0 for the first (:362) and == 0 for the plain one (:370); the assertion IS the difference between two toolchain configurations of the same source. The SHN_XINDEX arm generates a ~66,000-function source at run time (:376-380) purely to overflow e_shnum, compiles it (:384-385), and asserts readelf agrees the overflow happened (:391-392) before checking all three escapes (:396-398, :408, :412-419). Two further inputs are deliberately broken -- a 128-byte truncation (:425-427) and a non-ELF file (:436-437) -- and must raise (:434, :443). The 'gcc'/'g++' spawns are the test's own, so this is not product-api even though parseElfX86_64Object is reprobuild's.

The LINKAGE VARIANTS are the subject. buildProbe (:189) compiles one probe source four ways -- PIE (:237), non-PIE (:238) and -rdynamic (:242) -- against a real shared library (:185-186), and stripCopy (:244-256) runs real 'strip --strip-all' over two of them, asserting '.symtab' is present before and gone after so the arm cannot be vacuous. Every assertion is a COMPARISON ACROSS those variants: two different non-zero load biases in one process (:357-361), dlpi_addr == 0 for the non-PIE executable (:378), '.dynsym' answering for the stripped -rdynamic build (:496-506) while the same class is refused in the stripped build without it (:532-538). The stripped binaries and the stripped relocatable object with no tables at all (:644-651) are degenerate on purpose -- an edge that produced them would be a broken build. So are the five copies corrupted byte by byte at :622-639, whose whole point is that 'elf-object-malformed' must not surface as 'elf-symbol-not-found' (:692-702).

The LINKER's merging behaviour is the assertion. One gcc link (:105-108) joins two translation units that each define 'static int hcr_lx_ambiguous_helper', compiled with -ffunction-sections precisely because that is the configuration MOST favourable to design 7.4's st_shndx key. readelf confirms independently of the resolver that both definitions landed FUNC LOCAL under one name (:121-126) with both STT_FILE symbols present (:127-128), and the gate then asserts the two candidates share ONE output section index (:177-178) -- which is what makes the design's qualified form still ambiguous (:179-183). That property belongs to what ld did with the inputs, not to the artifact as an artifact: an edge naming the same two sources would still have to be re-measured here to establish it, and a toolchain that stopped merging would have to redden this gate rather than pass it silently.

MIGRATABLE, both halves, and neither needs C. The fixture exe is a fixed 3-line literal written at :413 with no substitution and compiled at :420; compileWindowsLauncher (:325, called at :353 and :450) nim c's the TRACKED apps/repro-launcher/repro_launcher.nim, which has no graph edge. Formerly dynamic-source on the strength of the word 'inline', but inline text that never varies is a checked-in fixture that has not been checked in.

MOVED DELIBERATELY, and the previous justification was accurate -- only the bucket was wrong. writeFixtureProvider (:38) concatenates seven MODULE-LEVEL CONSTS (:9-15), so the rendered text is invariant; the drift comes from compiling that one invariant source three times (:230, :304, :320) under different -d: defines. That is not 'text generated at run time', it is three build variants, which nim.c(defines = ...) expresses directly -- so a checked-in fixture plus three edges would work. Nim-only; nothing blocks it but the work.
